official.description_text:
Postdoctoral researcher in software technology
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
The work consists of:
designing and implementing software prototypes & demonstrators
participating to collaborative experiments in the context of software engineering research.
writing collaborative research papers & grant proposals
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
The candidate should have a strong background from at least one of the areas of formal verification and system security.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline.
A specificalization in software engineering, N-1.
Experience of research in a laboratory is a plus.
Experience with systems programming and computer security is an advantage.
Scientific skills.
Educational ability.
Awareness of diversity and equal treatment issues with a particular focus on gender equality.
Cooperation skills.
Independence.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.
Trade union representatives
Contact information to
trade union representatives.
To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.
A
position as a postdoctoral fellow
is a time-limited qualified appointment focusing mainly on research, intended as a first career step after a dissertation.
Other information
For
information about processing of personal data
in the recruitment process.

If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in software technology, emphasizing design and implementation of software prototypes and demonstrators, collaborative research experiments, and publication in software engineering. Focus areas include formal verification and system security.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic alignment. The position is pure software engineering focused on formal verification, system security, and systems programming. The researcher's themes are human-centred XR, collaborative immersive learning, spatial cognition, and social interaction. Formal verification and security are infrastructure and correctness concerns orthogonal to user experience, learning outcomes, or immersive system design. No overlap with target identity.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological fit. Position requires systems programming, formal verification, and security analysis—all theoretical and low-level. Researcher's methods are user-centred design, experimental psychology (spatial transfer), user studies, and iterative XR application development. The 'software prototyping and demonstrators' framing is superficially similar but serves entirely different purposes: here it's formal correctness and security; for researcher, it's experiential and educational outcomes. 'Collaborative experiments' language differs fundamentally.

growth_value.rationale: Limited growth value toward target identity. Position would deepen systems programming and formal reasoning skills, valuable for rigorous backend development. However, formal verification and security are not on the researcher's roadmap for human-centred immersive systems. Could support future infrastructure work for multiplayer XR (e.g., secure synchronization, verified protocols), but not directly. Opportunity cost is significant.

strategic_value.rationale: Low strategic value. Position is at KTH (target geography, Sweden) with two years' duration and reasonable funding stability. However, the software engineering group (formal verification, security) is orthogonal to HCI and immersive systems. Supervisor (Martin Monperrus) is a leading software engineering researcher but with no HCI, XR, or learning science background. The postdoc structure is standard, but the research trajectory diverges significantly from target identity. Geographic placement is positive; domain mismatch is significant.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD in relevant field or equivalence; researcher has MSc by Research in progress—major eligibility blocker unless completion is imminent before employment
Requires 'strong background from at least one of the areas of formal verification and system security'; researcher has no documented expertise in either area
Preferred: PhD obtained within last three years—not applicable; researcher is MSc candidate
'Research in a laboratory is a plus'; researcher has applied lab work (user studies) but not formal verification or security lab work
risks: PhD eligibility blocker; must hold PhD or be close to completion—researcher's MSc completion timeline is ambiguous
Domain expertise gap; no background in formal verification or security—steep learning curve with high failure risk
Career pivot risk; postdoc in software verification and security would further distance researcher from human-centred immersive systems research
Supervisor group (software engineering, formal methods) has no connection to HCI, XR, education, or user experience—poor mentorship for target identity
Publication record in HCI/XR may be misaligned with software engineering conference/journal expectations; cultural fit with publication venues unclear
